title: Canonical descent of one finitely presented module map over a directed preorder
statement: Let I be a directed preorder, F:I\to\mathrm{CRing} a functor, i_0\in I, and A=\operatorname{colim}F [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Let M,N be finitely presented F(i_0)-modules [def-sc-finitely-presented-module], and let f:A\otimes_{F(i_0)}M\to A\otimes_{F(i_0)}N be A-linear. Scalar extension means tensor product, with comparison isomorphisms induced by the extension-restriction adjunction [def-pod-ring-scalar-extension]. For i\ge i_0 let e_i(X):A\otimes_{F(i_0)}X\to A\otimes_{F(i)}(F(i)\otimes_{F(i_0)}X) be the canonical comparison, incorporating the colimit cocone equality and scalar-extension associativity. Then there is i\ge i_0 and an F(i)-linear g:F(i)\otimes_{F(i_0)}M\to F(i)\otimes_{F(i_0)}N satisfying e_i(N)^{-1}\circ(A\otimes_{F(i)}g)\circ e_i(M)=f. No complex, graded family, boundedness hypothesis, or differential compatibility is involved.

source.place: Tag 05N7 (2), the map clause; its finite presentation matrix argument, used in Perfect Tag 09RE affine case (1)

proof.text: Choose finite presentations of M and N. By [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-right-exact] and [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-finite-product], their scalar extensions have the corresponding finite presentation matrices over A and every stage ring. Express the images under f of the finitely many generators of M using the chosen generators of N. Express each image of a defining relation of M as a combination of the defining relations of N.

Using [lem-pc-filtered-colimit-commrings-elementwise], lift the finitely many image coefficients and relation-witness coefficients to stages and take a common upper bound with i0. Each entry of the matrix equation between these coefficients holds over A; the equality criterion makes it hold at a common later stage j. The generator images now kill the defining relations of M, hence determine an F(j)-linear map between the stage tensor products. Its further extension is f, as checked on generators. This uses only directed upper bounds and remains valid for preorders.

The canonical comparisons send 1 tensor x to 1 tensor (1 tensor x), by ModuleCat.extendScalarsComp_hom_app_one_tmul. Checking both sides on these tensors gives the conjugation equality; these tensors generate the extension as an A-module. Zero generators or relations, and zero rings or modules, cause no exception to the argument.

proof_origin.place: Tag 05N7 (2), explicit finite presentation coefficient proof and canonical comparison identification by W3

lean.statement:
theorem finitePresentation_map_directedColimit
    {I : Type u} [Preorder I] [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)]
    (F : I ⥤ CommRingCat.{u}) (i₀ : I) (M N : ModuleCat.{u} (F.obj i₀))
    (hM : Module.FinitePresentation (F.obj i₀) M)
    (hN : Module.FinitePresentation (F.obj i₀) N)
    (f : (extendScalars (colimit.ι F i₀).hom).obj M ⟶
      (extendScalars (colimit.ι F i₀).hom).obj N) :
    let e (i : Set.Ici i₀) (X : ModuleCat.{u} (F.obj i₀)) :=
      eqToIso (congrArg (fun r ↦ (extendScalars r).obj X)
        (congrArg CommRingCat.Hom.hom (colimit.w F (homOfLE i.property)).symm)) ≪≫
      (extendScalarsComp (F.map (homOfLE i.property)).hom (colimit.ι F i.val).hom).app X
    ∃ i : Set.Ici i₀,
      ∃ g : (extendScalars (F.map (homOfLE i.property)).hom).obj M ⟶
        (extendScalars (F.map (homOfLE i.property)).hom).obj N,
        (e i M).hom ≫ (extendScalars (colimit.ι F i.val).hom).map g ≫ (e i N).inv = f
